job.description: The one job, in one sentence.

kind.description: brick = a reusable package (early stage); system = a feature's end-to-end acceptance wired from bricks; change = one tracker issue or a batch of related issues (growth stage). Only items are measured; a feature or goal is never an item.

test.description: Same shape as commands.test in the config.

bench.description: Same shape as commands.bench in the config.

source.description: file:line in the project's build order this item comes from.

paths.description: More paths the item owns, beside `path`. A result holds at HEAD only while these, its dependencies' paths and the protected paths are unchanged; an item with no path is compared on the whole root.

purpose.description: What the item is for, in one sentence (sizing note when it joins two jobs).

hides.description: What the item hides behind its interface.

interface.description: What it takes, returns and raises, in one line.

consumers.description: Who uses it (item ids or named callers).

fits.description: true when the tool does the job (a sizing note: why a package?).

est_loc.description: Estimated lines of code; compared with config sizing (a note, never a gate).

refs.description: Tracker refs this item resolves (e.g. #123); a fact the item carries, read by nothing yet.

context.description: Citations of the exact spec passages the item needs, as {path, lines: "a-b"}; never copied text. work_packet extracts them into the work packet.

rules.description: Catalog rule ids that apply to the item; printed in its work packet.

split_from.description: Id of the item this one was split from. Children own disjoint paths taken from the parent's; the parent keeps its targets and depends on every child, so it is measured after them.

embodies.description: Catalog rule ids the item satisfies by being used (class embodied); judgment rules of its users leave them out.

split_kind.description: Why a split child was cut (SPIDR): spike, path, interface, data or rules. A child without one is listed as a fact.
